pr.title: In `simplify_repeated_aggregate`, don't test first element against itself
pr.description:
r? @saethlin 
Noticed that in `InstSimplifyContext::simplify_repeated_aggregate`, we're accidentally evaluating the first element's value twice, and then comparing it with itself, instead of just checking whether the rest of the elements are equal to the first one.
This will probably save very few cycles, but since `InstSimplify` is always enabled, this might improve perf by a bit.

pr.author: yotamofek

processing.reason: The PR change is purely a redundant-work optimization, not a semantics-changing transformation. Historical `simplify_repeated_aggregate` checked `fields.iter().all(...)`, which includes index 0; because the first field was already evaluated into `first_val`, that entry trivially evaluates equal to itself and the comparison always succeeds. The merged version splits off `first` and checks `rest.iter().all(...)`, covering exactly the same semantic condition for fields 1..n. Both versions accept and rewrite exactly the same uniform-constant array aggregates and reject the same non-uniform/non-constant ones; the only difference is one extra pure constant evaluation and self-comparison. The frozen analysis itself labels this an optimization with unchanged emitted results. Since constant evaluation is pure and the task forbids adding arbitrary return-value changes, observable side effects, or unrelated rewrites, no source-grounded pair can satisfy the requirement that original and transformed functions produce different defined values on identical inputs. A fabricated difference would not represent this historical PR.

analysis.originalLogic: `InstSimplifyContext::simplify_repeated_aggregate` matched an array aggregate and required at least five fields, then took the first field with `let first = &fields[rustc_abi::FieldIdx::ZERO];`, evaluated that first constant into `first_val`, and checked uniformity with `fields.iter().all(|field| { ... })`. Because the iterator still included index zero, the first constant was looked up and evaluated a second time inside the closure and then compared with `first_val`, i.e. the first element was tested against itself.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical implementation did not separate the first field from the rest: it used the whole `fields` slice in the uniformity check (`if fields.iter().all(|field| { ... })`). That is semantically equivalent to checking only fields 1..n because the first field trivially evaluates equal to `first_val`, but it performs redundant work (re-evaluating the first constant and comparing it against itself). The corrected transformation borrows the aggregate as `&*rvalue`, splits it with `let (first, rest) = fields[..].split_first().unwrap();`, and checks only `rest.iter().all(...)`. This is an optimization/elimination of redundant self-comparison, not a change to the emitted semantic result.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR `Rvalue::Aggregate` whose `AggregateKind` is `Array(_)`, with at least five fields (the pass returns early when `fields.len() < 5`), where the first field is an `Operand::Constant` whose `const_.eval(self.tcx, self.typing_env, first.span)` succeeds, and where the remaining fields are examined as possible constant operands for equality with the first evaluated value.
analysis.summary: In InstSimplify's repeated-array-aggregate simplification, the original code checked every field including the first, so the first constant was evaluated twice and compared with itself. The merged change splits off the first field and checks only the rest. This is a redundant-work optimization with unchanged results; it is not a confirmed correctness bug fix.
analysis.trigger: An array aggregate with at least five constant elements, especially one whose elements are all equal, reaches `simplify_repeated_aggregate` during InstSimplify. The pass then checks whether all elements equal the first evaluated constant.
preconditions: The rvalue must match `Rvalue::Aggregate(box AggregateKind::Array(_), fields)`; other aggregate kinds are ignored.
`fields.len()` must be at least 5, because the pass bails out before examining elements otherwise.
The first field must be `Operand::Constant` and `first.const_.eval(...)` must succeed.
Every field that is checked must be `Operand::Constant` whose evaluated value equals `first_val`; any non-constant or unequal field rejects the rewrite.
The array length guard makes `fields[..].split_first().unwrap()` safe; the split must retain the first element separately from the rest.
pitfalls: Testing the whole `fields` slice in `all(...)` still includes index zero, producing a trivial self-comparison and redundant constant evaluation.
Splitting with `split_first()` must not lose any real element: the uniform check must cover `rest`, i.e. indices 1..n, after the first is handled separately.
Do not apply this reasoning to `Rvalue::Repeat`; this pass specifically matches array aggregates with explicit fields.
Do not treat the change as fixing wrong optimized output: both versions accept exactly the same uniform-constant arrays and reject the same non-uniform/non-constant ones.
The `fields.len() < 5` early return is what makes the `unwrap()` on `split_first()` safe; removing or reordering that guard would introduce a panic path.
Borrowing via `&*rvalue` is needed so the fields can be borrowed immutably and split while the `Rvalue` remains the same object; this is an implementation detail rather than a semantic condition.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused MIR optimization tests rather than runtime tests. Construct a function returning an array aggregate with at least five identical `const` elements (e.g. `[1, 1, 1, 1, 1]`) and check the optimized MIR: the repeated elements should be recognized uniformly and simplified (for example to a repeat-style form) by InstSimplify. Add a negative case with one differing element (e.g. `[1, 1, 1, 1, 2]`) and verify no uniform-array rewrite occurs. Add boundary cases for exactly 4 equal elements (below the `fields.len() < 5` guard) and for a field that is not an `Operand::Constant`, both of which must be left unchanged. Because the supplied patch contains only the `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/instsimplify.rs` hunk and no visible regression-test edits, these cases must be authored separately; no execution or reproduction is claimed.
evidence: In `simplify_repeated_aggregate`, don't test first element against itself
we're accidentally evaluating the first element's value twice, and then comparing it with itself, instead of just checking whether the rest of the elements are equal to the first one.
This will probably save very few cycles, but since `InstSimplify` is always enabled, this might improve perf by a bit.
